name: 1973 OPEC Oil Embargo
notes: Arab oil embargo on US/allies after Yom Kippur War. Pre-1986: use OWID annual series, not daily EIA.

name: 1979 Iranian Revolution
notes: Iranian oil production collapsed during revolution. Pre-1986: use OWID annual series.

name: 1980 Iran-Iraq War
notes: War knocked out both countries' exports simultaneously. Pre-1986: use OWID annual series.

name: 1986 Saudi 'Yamani Flood' (Price War)
notes: CAVEAT: true onset was late 1985, before our clean daily series starts (1986-01-02) -- the 'before' price here is already partway into the crash, not a clean pre-event baseline. Kept in deliberately as an honest example of a data-boundary limitation, not hidden.

name: 1990 Gulf War (Iraq invades Kuwait)
notes: Kuwaiti + Iraqi exports removed from market; refine supply_loss_pct against actual EIA mbd figures.

name: 1997-98 Asian Financial Crisis
notes: Thai baht collapse triggered an Asian demand crash, made worse by OPEC raising quotas 10% right beforehand on the wrong assumption demand would keep growing -- prices fell toward $10/barrel by end of 1998.

name: 2002-03 Venezuela PDVSA General Strike
notes: Political/labor strike (not armed conflict) shut down PDVSA for ~2 months, removing an estimated 2.3 million bpd from world supply at its worst.

name: 2003 Iraq War
notes: Smaller supply disruption than 1990; market was better supplied overall.

name: 2005 Hurricane Katrina
notes: Pure natural-disaster refinery/production shut-in, zero geopolitical conflict -- good test of whether the model over-relies on conflict_intensity rather than actual supply loss.

name: 2008 Global Financial Crisis (Lehman Collapse)
notes: Demand collapsed in the recession, but the earlier run-up to $147/barrel was also partly a speculative bubble -- price move is hard to explain from supply/demand features alone. Good 'messy' example on purpose.

name: 2011 Libyan Civil War
notes: Libyan output (~1.6 mbd) largely offline for months.

name: 2012 EU Oil Embargo on Iran
notes: Sanctions removed roughly 1 million bpd of Iranian exports from the market -- a slow-building sanctions event rather than a sudden shock.

name: 2014 OPEC Refuses to Cut Output (Price War Begins)
notes: OPEC chose not to cut output despite falling prices; Brent fell from $77.75 the day before the meeting to $70.15 the day after. Market share war vs US shale.

name: 2016 OPEC Vienna Agreement (First Cut Since 2008)
notes: Calm, negotiated 1.2 million bpd supply cut, zero conflict -- WTI rose 9.6% same day. Lowest conflict_intensity in the table; balances the war-driven events.

name: 2018 US Reimposes Iran Sanctions (JCPOA Withdrawal)
notes: Trump withdrew from the JCPOA in May 2018; sanctions took full effect Nov 4. Iranian exports fell from ~2.5 million bpd toward ~1 million bpd over the following months.

name: 2019 Abqaiq-Khurais Drone Attack
notes: Very short-lived (days) despite large headline supply-loss %; good test of how fast markets price in a rapid recovery.

name: 2020 COVID Demand Collapse + Saudi-Russia Price War
notes: OPEC+ talks collapsed same week lockdowns began; global oil demand fell by as much as 29 million bpd (~30% of demand) in April 2020. WTI later went negative on Apr 20, 2020 -- a separate, even more extreme event you could add on its own.

name: 2021 Texas Winter Storm Uri
notes: Second zero-conflict natural-disaster event, but a different cause than Katrina (grid failure/freeze-offs, not storm damage) -- shut in an estimated 2-4 million bpd of US crude production at the peak.

name: 2022 Russia invades Ukraine
notes: Sanctions phased in over following months rather than an instant cutoff -- consider using a delayed supply_loss ramp.

name: 2022 US Strategic Petroleum Reserve Release
notes: NOT a crisis itself -- a deliberate government COUNTERMEASURE responding to the Russia-Ukraine crisis (180 million barrels released over 6 months, ~1 million bpd average). Useful contrast: how much does a policy response dampen a price move versus the shock alone.

name: 2023 Israel-Hamas War Begins
notes: Minimal direct supply loss but elevated geopolitical risk premium -- useful as a 'intensity without supply loss' data point.

name: 2023 Houthi Red Sea Attacks Begin
notes: Shipping reroutes around Cape of Good Hope rather than production loss -- tests the detour_days feature in isolation.

name: 2025 Israel-Iran '12-Day War'
notes: Brent jumped from $69.36 to $74.23 overnight, but analysts confirmed no actual physical disruption to oil flows during this conflict -- pure risk premium, like the 2023 Israel-Hamas row. Good contrast case.

name: 2026 US-Israel War on Iran (Hormuz Blockade)
notes: ROUGH ESTIMATE, still unfolding as of Sept 2026 -- refine as more data emerges. Iran imposed an actual blockade on shipping through the Strait (unlike the 2025 conflict). Brent rose 8% within days ($71.32 -> $77.24) and later broke $100. Unlike Suez/Red Sea, ships cannot detour around a closed Hormuz -- there is no sea route out of the Gulf -- so detour_days does not really apply here; treat this as a structural limitation of the current feature set, not a data entry of 0 meaning 'no cost'.
